candidates.title: Editorial-technical register
candidates.one_line_contract: Editorial-technical register: asymmetric editorial composition fused with precise product-tech detailing, one restrained accent
candidates.portable_contract: compose asymmetrically with strong column structure, deliberate negative space, and offset alignment — never a centered generic hero stack; two typographic voices — one expressive display voice for headline moments, one quiet utility voice (clean sans or mono) for labels, steps, timestamps, and metadata; engineer the surface with fine rules, grid traces, thin borders, and small technical markers; treat media as narrative bands — wide strips or inset panels crossing the grid in controlled ways; one restrained accent used only to punctuate (active states, key figures, current step, primary action); hold the register midpoint — more narrative than a dashboard, more precise than a magazine. Tuning axes (vocabulary, never lint): composition drama · instrumentation density · accent sparsity · media weight.
candidates.context_boundary: developer/technical products, research and documentation, editorially presented case studies, restrained light or dark neutral surfaces.
candidates.anti_context: care/health and consumer-warm surfaces; urgent task flows; operational/status panels and dense data tables — these stay plain.

candidates.title: Paper-technical light register
candidates.one_line_contract: Paper-technical light register: warm paper surfaces in a dark outer frame with bracketed technical geometry
candidates.portable_contract: build primary surfaces on warm off-white paper tones, never stark white; frame the light interior in a darker outer shell so content reads placed and intentional; add quiet technical structure — thin borders, inset rules, small corner brackets, restrained fine diagonal texture on large fields; one crisp accent for active states and focal details while warm neutrals carry the interface; keep outer shells softly rounded but inner layout logic crisp; calm motion only. Tuning axes: paper warmth · framing strength · roundness · accent intensity · texture amount.
candidates.context_boundary: light-mode technical/product surfaces wanting warmth and tactility — memos, catalogues, documentation.
candidates.anti_context: dense data tables and statutory/spec surfaces (no texture, no warm-tint contrast loss, no bracket ornament there); urgent flows; any surface where texture threatens legibility.

candidates.title: Documentary-brutalist genre playbook
candidates.one_line_contract: Documentary-brutalist genre playbook: billboard type, black/white chapters, documentary collage, accessible disclosure controls
candidates.portable_contract: open with a billboard-scale positioning line and minimal navigation; alternate hard black chapters (large titles, role labels, documentary media) with sparse warm-white thinking chapters; one compressed display face paired with one neutral grotesk; exposed grid, square corners; no glass, glow, or decorative gradients; line breaks are composition — verify at every breakpoint; one documentary collage as a paced process story: reserve every image box before load, keep DOM order narrative even when the visual grid is irregular, cap parallax below 5%, captions on hover AND focus, grid survives failed media; pale proof surfaces only for verified quotes; disclosure controls semantic and accessible (aria-expanded, no focus traps outside true modals); oversized footer wordmark.
candidates.context_boundary: agencies, studios, cultural institutions, portfolios, investigations — surfaces earning a strong point of view.
candidates.anti_context: forms, checkout, help, appendices, and any care/consumer-warm or urgent surface — calm, legible, conventional treatment there.

candidates.title: Brutalist contextual motion band
candidates.one_line_contract: Brutalist contextual band: 160–220 ms controls, 500–760 ms masks/entrances, parallax <5%, one transition at a time
candidates.portable_contract: controls answer in 160–220 ms; masks and section entrances take 500–760 ms; animate one reading transition at a time; slow collage parallax capped below 5%; prefer decisive cuts over floating; pause offscreen observers and media, clean up route timelines; never smooth-scroll theater or scroll hijack.
candidates.anti_context: forms and dense operational surfaces — instant feedback only, zero entrance choreography.
candidates.inclusion_reason: personas carry zero numeric timing DNA

candidates.title: Product-proof state band
candidates.one_line_contract: Product-proof band: 160–220 ms controls, 420–700 ms state changes, 45–70 ms card stagger, one handoff at a time
candidates.portable_contract: control feedback 160–220 ms; interface state changes 420–700 ms; card stagger 45–70 ms; animate one handoff at a time; background drift slow, optional, offscreen-paused; no fake typing, perpetual floating, or decorative loops; render settled UI immediately under reduced motion.
candidates.inclusion_reason: personas carry zero numeric timing DNA

candidates.title: Cinematic scrub calibration
candidates.one_line_contract: Cinematic scrub calibration: scrub 0.8–1.4, reveal at ~82% viewport, smooth-scroll lerp ~0.08, word stagger 35–70 ms
candidates.portable_contract: scroll-scrub factor 0.8–1.4 for cinematic delay; reveals trigger when an element's top crosses roughly 82% of the viewport; smooth-scroll interpolation around 0.08; word stagger 35–70 ms, line stagger 80–140 ms, card stagger 60–100 ms; staggered motion guides reading order, never decorates it.
candidates.anti_context: utility blocks, search/index surfaces, tables, forms — native scrolling, instant anchors, no scrub; reduced motion renders the settled story.

candidates.title: Number details
candidates.one_line_contract: Two-digit numeric detail markers as quiet secondary structure on ordered content
candidates.portable_contract: two-digit markers (01, 02, 03) as secondary architecture on genuinely ordered content; predictable positions — card corners, section gutters, timeline rails, beside headings; quiet mono or narrow uppercase at low contrast; consistent spacing and alignment across all marks; one numbering style per section; markers never compete with headings or actions.
candidates.context_boundary: ordered narrative sections — processes, chapters, chronologies.
candidates.anti_context: unordered content, statements/appendices/logs (which keep their own identifiers), urgent flows, error and legal surfaces.

candidates.title: Container lines and corner marks
candidates.one_line_contract: Container guide lines: 1 px low-opacity vertical edges + small corner squares, consistent per page
candidates.portable_contract: 1 px low-opacity vertical guides at the exact content-container edges; small square marks (~6 px) at corners or section intersections; one consistent container width per page; guides behind content, above background, pointer-transparent; strong-opacity variant reserved for deliberate emphasis.
candidates.context_boundary: structured editorial/technical layouts needing quiet measurement tension.
candidates.anti_context: inside dense data tables, reading panes, forms; urgent flows.

candidates.title: Progressive edge blur
candidates.one_line_contract: Progressive edge blur: stepped backdrop blur bands masked from a viewport edge, pointer-transparent
candidates.portable_contract: a stepped blur band fixed at one viewport edge (top or bottom), built from layered backdrop blurs with graduated masks so blur strength ramps smoothly; band height ~10–15% of viewport; pointer-transparent; above content, below modals; requires real content behind it to blur.
candidates.context_boundary: long reading or narrative surfaces where edge softening aids focus.
candidates.anti_context: must never overlay focusable controls, forms, or the reading measure; not on urgent flows; drop the device entirely rather than compromise legibility.

candidates.title: Scroll-progress timeline
candidates.one_line_contract: Scroll-progress timeline: semantic ordered steps with compositor-scaled progress line and active-step state
candidates.portable_contract: the sequence is a semantic ordered list with real headings first — line, dots, and active states only enhance it; quiet base line behind all points, one progress line scaled on the compositor (scaleY/scaleX, transform-origin at start); measure from first to last step centers and normalize scroll between them; recalc geometry after fonts, images, resize, orientation, mutation; mark the active step (aria-current="step" only when meaningful; never announce every scroll tick); alternate layout only with balanced width, left rail for long copy, horizontal only for short keyboard-safe sequences; collapse to a left rail on small screens preserving reading order.
candidates.context_boundary: genuinely ordered multi-step content — guides, explainers, chaptered studies.
candidates.anti_context: short single-screen sections, FAQs, contact blocks, non-sequential content — no rail, no progress ornament.

candidates.title: Role-to-ratio and text-reserve media contract
candidates.one_line_contract: Role→ratio media contract with 30–50% text-reserve on wide imagery and focal-safety rules
candidates.portable_contract: declare a role for every image before selection, and let role fix ratio — avatar 1:1 (256/512/1024 square exports); headshot 4:5 or 3:4, shoulders-up, faces centered; wide hero/background 16:9 with calm negative space; story/mobile 9:16; on wide imagery carrying text, reserve 30–50% of the frame as calm space for the message; keep faces' eyes in the upper third, never crop chin or forehead, preserve horizon lines; verify focal and text safety at 390/768/1440, not by file ratio alone; provide resolution variants per role.
candidates.context_boundary: surfaces with supplied or role-approved imagery — campaigns, editorial, product launches.
candidates.anti_context: data, legal, console, and form surfaces get no decorative imagery; the contract never justifies inventing an image — intentional no-image is a first-class outcome.

candidates.title: Portrait narrative register
candidates.one_line_contract: Portrait narrative register: deliberate functional-headshot vs editorial-portrait choice per context
candidates.portable_contract: choose deliberately between two portrait registers and state the choice per context — functional headshot (neutral background, shoulders-up, professional-warm; for org, directory, executive contexts) versus editorial portrait (environmental, candid, narrative; for story and interview contexts); one register per context, never mixed within one; register choice is content design, not decoration.
candidates.context_boundary: people-centered surfaces — profiles, biographies, interviews, teams.
candidates.anti_context: compliance/ID/verification and uniform directory or press-kit contexts require the functional register; editorial treatment there is a leak.
candidates.inclusion_reason: personas cannot demand a photo register
